title: Visual Basic 5/6 program structure
description: The header, project data and objects of a Visual Basic 5/6 program, read out of the file. This is the project's shape rather than its code: the shape is the same whether the program was compiled to native x86 or to p-code, and the structures that would give a method's code are filled in only by the compiler that needs them.

file.description: Path of the program as it was given.

header.description: The VB5! structure the program's entry point pushes before calling ThunRTMain.

signature.description: Always VB5!, including in a VB6 program.

rva.description: Where the header is, relative to the image base.

language_dll.description: The language DLL the program asks for. VB6 writes * for a language-neutral program, which is what every program measured here does.

sub_main_rva.description: The procedure the runtime calls after it starts, or 0 when a form is shown instead.

isa.description: x86 for a natively compiled program, vb6-pcode for one that is interpreted.

data_size.description: Size of the per-object data the runtime allocates.

native_code_rva.description: Where native code starts, or 0 for a p-code program: the aNativeCode field.

build_path.description: The path the program was built in, recorded by the compiler in UTF-16. Machine names, drive letters and the source layout of the original build, straight out of the file.

objects_declared.description: Objects the project's object table declares.

objects_reported.description: Objects actually read; fewer than declared only when something was unreadable, which is then in problems.

objects_compiled.description: Objects the table says were compiled. Not always equal to the number it declares: ElementEvil.exe says 76 against 73, so the two are not one number written twice.

code_note.description: What the tool can do with this program's code, said rather than implied.

objects.description: One entry per form, class module and standard module, in the order the object table lists them.

name.description: The object's name as the project spells it. Empty when the name pointer does not land on readable text, which is reported in problems.

kind.description: form, class module, standard module, user control, property page, or the raw type word when it is none of those.

type_flags.description: The type word itself: 0x00018083 is a form, 0x00018001 a standard module, 0x00118003 a class module.

methods.description: Methods the object declares, from its descriptor.

problems.description: Anything the program's own pointers said that did not add up, said out loud rather than dropped.
